newsitem.title: CANADA: CP seeks buyer for Ontario rail shortline.
newsitem.headline: CP seeks buyer for Ontario rail shortline.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd unit Canadian Pacific Railway Co (CPR) said on Wednesday that it is seeking a buyer for its Sudbury-Sault Ste. Marie route in the Canadian province of Ontario.

"Given the interest in Ontario railroading shown so far by the shortline industry, we're confident we can find a new operator who will maintain a reliable and low-cost regional link to the CPR core network well into the next century," said Gil Mackie, of the railway's Secondary Network Restructuring group, in a statement.
Calls for expressions of interest have gone out to potential new operators across North America and a number of positive responses have been received, he said.
Operation of the former CPR Sudbury-Smiths Falls route in Ontario was recently turned over to an Edmonton-based shortline company under a long-term lease arrangement.
"Since that line was transferred service levels have exceeded targets and our customers have been pleased with the local switching service," Mackie said.

Normal freight service (there are no passenger trains) along the 292-kilometre (181-mile) Sudbury-Sault Ste. Marie line will continue during negotiations, CPR said. A 60-kilometre (38-mile) connecting line at McKerrow branches southwest to Espanola and the Whitefish Falls area.

Known as the Webbwood and Little Current subdivisions, the two lines serve the steel, resource and forest-product industries, with connections to the CPR core network at Sudbury and other railways at Sault Ste. Marie. The transfer to a new operator is expected to take place by mid-1997, the company said.
"The Sudbury-Sault route has an international connection and a traffic base that looks ready to grow over the next several years," Mackie said.
